title: Volume 1 Bonus Story: The Tsundere Childhood Friend Feels Lonely
content: [img]../image/m271.jpg

This was before my childhood friends made the job change to yandere. It was a rare day when Setsuna and Arisa were both together, and they had promised Ijuuin and our classmates to take cosplay photos of the childhood friends after school.
“Sorry, you two. It suddenly turned into a cosplay photoshoot plan,” I said as I walked home alongside Setsuna and Arisa that day.
“It’s not a big deal. It’s not the first time you’ve come crying to us, Kazuma,” Arisa replied.
“Remember when the uncles got transferred overseas? That was crazy. The aunt was chasing after Kazukun with a face like a yakuza. I was shocked,” Setsuna added.
“Yeah, that was intense. I even dreamed about that aunt sprinting at me with a hemp rope in hand...” Arisa said.
“Can you stop with that story? It’s a trauma for me,” I said.

The two of them were happily chatting with me sandwiched in between, but for me, that was a black history moment. I wanted to forget it as soon as possible and not recall it, so I immediately decided to change the subject.
“Ah, Arisa. By the way, good job at the last live show. I haven’t properly praised you yet, but it was really great. The best,” I said.
“Ah, thanks. But Setsuna worked hard too, so why don’t you praise her as well?” Arisa said, looking away shyly. She’s still not straightforward, I thought with a wry smile, and continued.
“No, I already praised Setsuna. Right?” I asked.
“Yeah. I got a lot of praise the day after the live♪ Oh, and we promised to get new smartphones, didn’t we?” Setsuna said.
“Huh?”
“Yeah, that’s right. I forgot because of all the recent commotion,” I admitted.
“When should we go buy them? Golden Week’s a bit busy with the live, but after that...” I started.
“W-wait a minute!” Arisa interrupted, cutting into the conversation as Setsuna and I exchanged glances.
“Hm? What’s up?” I asked.
“W-what do you mean by getting new smartphones? I haven’t heard anything about that,” Arisa said.
“Oh, right. I didn’t tell Arisa. On the day Ijuuin transferred in, I told Setsuna I wanted a new smartphone,” I explained.
“So we decided to get new ones together. We want to have the same model, after all,” Setsuna added.
“Well, that’s the story... What’s with that face, Arisa?” I asked.
She was glaring at me with a deadpan look.
“Nothing. It’s nothing,” she said.
“No, it doesn’t look like nothing. You look obviously upset...” I said.
“I’m just as usual. Don’t worry about it. I’m not mad that you’re prioritizing Setsuna or anything. Absolutely not,” Arisa said, turning her eyes away with a pout. It was clear she was bothered.
“R-really?” I asked.
“Really. So just go ahead and buy new phones together with Setsuna. I’m totally! Completely! Not! Bothered!” she said.
“O-okay. Got it,” I said.
Uh-oh, she’s sulking. She seems to think she’s being left out. Come to think of it, Arisa has always hated being treated like an outcast and is quite lonely. I had forgotten that. My mistake.
“Um, sorry. That wasn’t my intention at all,” I said.
“I know that already. You don’t have to say it over and over. I’m not trying to get in your way. Do whatever you want,” she said.
It was too late to patch things up. Arisa had completely dug in her heels, and there was no way to reach her.
Hmm, this is tough. Trying to persuade her now would probably backfire. I need to change the flow, but I’m not the right person for that.
(Then it’s got to be...)
I glanced sideways at Setsuna walking beside me. The one to rely on was naturally the other childhood friend here.
Luckily, Setsuna immediately noticed my gaze. She looked at me sideways with a happy expression, but I wanted to avoid Arisa noticing. Without a word, I tried to communicate with eye contact.
(Setsuna, please somehow cheer Arisa up.)
I blinked repeatedly to convey my will.
Normally, this wouldn’t work, but conveniently, my childhood friends aren’t normal. They always put me first and understand me better than anyone—even more than my parents.
So, even without words, my feelings should get through!
Believing that, I stared intently at my black-haired childhood friend, and soon Setsuna nodded happily.
(Oh, it got through!)
As expected of Setsuna! That’s why she’s the childhood friend who will support me for life!
I was about to make a victorious fist pump from the joy of successful communication when—
“You want money, Kazukun! If you don’t have enough, you should’ve said so earlier!” Setsuna exclaimed.
Nope, that’s not what I meant at all.
“Setsuna, no, that’s not it,” I said.
“Wait here! I’ll go to the convenience store right now!” she said.
I tried to stop her in a panic, but Setsuna was too quick. She flicked her skirt and dashed off to the convenience store before I could stop her.
“Ah, geez...” I sighed, watching my childhood friend’s retreating back.
She understood, but not in the way I wanted. I was painfully reminded of the world’s truth and cruelty—that people really need to say things out loud for their true feelings to be understood.
“You’re relying on Setsuna again, not me,” a quiet, lonely voice reached my ears. I turned around to see Arisa standing still.
“Arisa...” I said.
“Am I really that unreliable? I’m not as straightforward as Setsuna, and maybe you find me annoying... but I’m trying my best in my own way,” she said, looking down.
I couldn’t see her expression, but I could guess what kind of face she was making.
I slowly took a step toward Arisa.
“Hey, don’t sulk.”
“Shut up. I’m not sulking. I’m not a kid. I’m way more responsible than you, Kazuma,” she said in a low, gloomy tone.
That didn’t sound convincing, but I didn’t comment on it. I just stopped in front of her.
“I know. I rely on you and I’m grateful. Before and after becoming an idol, I think I know better than anyone how hard you’ve been working,” I said sincerely.
That was the truth. Not a lie.
“Then why...” she started.
“That’s why I said I rely on you,” I interrupted, placing my hand on her head.
“Because of that, I sometimes forget you’re a girl the same age as me,” I said, gently stroking her head. The texture was just as soft as in the morning.
“Ah...” she whispered.
“I know a lot of your good points too. Sure, it’s easier to ask Setsuna, but don’t compare yourself to her and get depressed. That’s not like you,” I said.
“...Shut up,” she muttered.
“Don’t believe me? Then I’ll list your good points. First, you’re good at cooking. You’re thoughtful, a good singer, great at housework, caring, and cute...” I started counting on my fingers.
“Shut up, shut up, shut up! You don’t have to say stuff like that! It’s embarrassing!” Arisa shouted, trying to stop me.
Seeing her like that, I smiled inwardly. This was the Arisa Tsukishiro I knew well.
“Come on, I’m just telling the truth. You’re an idol, so you get praised all the time,” I said.
“I hate hearing it directly! Especially from you, Kazuma!” she said, then turned away. She must have been really embarrassed.
“Hey, cheer up,” I said.
“Ugh...” she groaned.
“Just so you know, when we go to buy new phones, I’m planning to invite you too. We’re not going to leave you out,” I said, deciding it was time to bring up the original topic.
She twitched her shoulder and looked at me cautiously.
“...Really?” she asked.
“Of course. I admit I forgot to tell you, but trust us more,” I said.
“You wouldn’t understand unless I said it, you idiot,” Arisa said, looking away with a flushed face. Maybe she finally realized how childish her attitude had been.
“By the way, I haven’t eaten your cooking lately. Make some for me again,” I said.
But better not touch that topic. I’d long since learned it’s best not to say unnecessary things to these childhood friends.
“What do you want to eat?” I asked.
“Hmm, probably curry. I still like it,” she said.
“You haven’t changed your tastes. You’re not a kid anymore,” I said.
“Whatever. I’m not going to change. And of course, I don’t plan to work. I’m going to live being supported for life,” I said.
“...You mean by us?” Arisa asked.
“Who else? We made a promise, remember?” I said.
It’s better to have more people supporting me, but right now, there’s no one else besides these two.
“A promise, huh. Yeah, we did make one. How nostalgic...” Arisa said.
“As long as you remember, it’s fine. I’ll definitely be supported. Otherwise, I can’t live,” I said.
“I know... but, hehe,” Arisa’s lips suddenly curved into a smile. It was the first expression she’d shown since the topic started, but I didn’t quite get why now.
“Why are you laughing? There wasn’t anything funny,” I said.
“Nothing. I just thought you really haven’t changed since way back then,” she said.
“What’s wrong with that?” I asked.
“Nope. You’re fine just the way you are. You’re troublesome and a pain, but that’s how you are, and that lets me be me too,” Arisa said with a soft smile.
“...Are you subtly making fun of me?” I asked.
“Who knows? I don’t mean to,” she said.
That sarcastic tone was exactly my childhood friend’s. Looks like she’s back to her usual self.
Feeling relieved inside, I saw Setsuna approaching from the corner of my eye. She must have returned from the convenience store.
“Arisa-chan, you’re in a better mood,” Setsuna said.
“Well, sort of,” Arisa nodded.
I nodded too. Honestly, I thought it would have settled sooner if Setsuna had been here, but since we managed on our own, I wouldn’t complain.
“Hehe, it was good you two talked alone. Arisa-chan isn’t straightforward, you know,” Setsuna said cheerfully.
Her words struck a chord.
“Hm? Setsuna, do you maybe understand...” I started to ask.
“Hey, Kazuma! What are you doing? Let’s go!” Setsuna pulled me along forcefully.
I was about to ask Setsuna, but she yanked my hand.
“Arisa said she wants curry. We’re going to the supermarket now, so at least carry the bags,” she said.
She marched ahead at a brisk pace, making it hard to keep step. If I relaxed, I might trip.
“Wait, calm down. There’s no need to rush like that,” I said.
“No! I want to do this now!” Arisa said, happily pulling my hand. Setsuna followed behind, giggling softly.
My childhood friends, unchanged since long ago.
“Haah, can’t be helped...” I sighed.
“Hey, Kazuma.”
“Hm?”
Though she’s now a beautiful idol, even so—
“I know you better than anyone, Kazuma!” Arisa said with a beaming smile.
Looking at her, I somehow felt our relationship would never change.
“Hehe, Arisa-chan’s in a good mood. If she becomes more honest, you two will get even closer... ufufu...”
...A few days later, after repeating exchanges that felt like déjà vu, I’d get into serious trouble in many ways, but that’s another story.
“Hehe, you’re really an idiot,”
Kazuma hasn’t changed at all since way back. Saying things like he wants to be supported or that he can’t live without you—things most people would never say—he says them without hesitation.
I really think he’s hopeless. But I’m the same.
When Kazuma seeks me out, I’m happy. When he says he needs me, I’m really happy.
That’s why I can work hard at being an idol... I think Setsuna feels the same.

Besides, I’ve known for a long time. Kazuma supports the Damenzu more than anyone. He came to our very first live when we had almost no fans. He cheers for us on his personal blog and always checks every live.
He’s an idiot, but he watches over us properly, needs us, and says we’re important. I think I... don’t hate him for that... ugh.
I hate that I can’t be honest even inside. So—this is something I could never say face to face, and never will—but thank you for staying with me despite my stubbornness, Kazuma!
